name: Robustness of the per-history calibrated waiting rules to recovery errors of the B3 model
reason: In the waiting simulations B3 is both the plant and the source of the rules' calibration: fixed waits and all thresholds are chosen on B3 outcomes, the current and smoothed kernels map the reporter to B3 success labels, and the B3 belief weights B3 trajectories. No rule is model-free; the B3 belief differs from the smoothed rule by its command-history likelihood. The measured mixed-protocol probe (60 min after a 30-min command at 25 ng/ml: median rise 4.1% of the naive rise, B3 31%) and the collapse of the B3 weights on measured cells (effective sample size 1.0-1.4) indicate that B3 overestimates recovery after a long command and that measured reporters leave the posterior's support. This study quantifies, before any experiment, how much recovery error the calibrated rules tolerate, whether an error the reporter reveals is handled better than one it hides, and whether recalibration against true outcomes restores the per-history reliability requirement.
unchanged: Simulation tables (results/b3/readiness_tables.npz), 25 ng/ml commands, 3- and 30-min previous commands, 5-min probe, decision grid 0-120 min in 2-min steps, W = 20 min, kappa = 0.5, failure penalty 140 min; estimators of readiness protocol version 3 (current; smoothed with scales 2, 4, 8, 16 min; B3 belief, key 'history' in the outputs, likelihood s.d. max(noise, 0.001)); fine threshold grid 0.50-0.99; per-history calibration as in b3_waiting_frontier (one parameter set per previous command, smallest calibration mean completion of that history subject to its calibration success >= target, ties as in that study; fixed waits one per history); calibration samples as references, each left out of its own references; the 20 calibration/evaluation splits and observation draws of the robustness study; observation noise s.d. 0.005 and 0.01; calibration targets 0.90, 0.92 and 0.94; evaluation against 0.9 for each history. Plant outcomes enter only the scoring (rule options and oracle); estimator references always use the model's trajectories and outcomes.
known_before_freezing: Readiness is monotone in the decision time for every sample and history. Readiness onset after the 30-min command (never ready = +infinity) has quantiles 78/82/88/98/106 min (10/25/50/75/90%); 15 of 1000 samples never become ready; onsets after the two commands correlate at 0.95. Oracle success within 120 min after the 30-min command over all samples under a hidden lag L: 0.985, 0.975, 0.961, 0.955, 0.938, 0.919, 0.896 at L = 0, 4, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 min and 0.31 at 35.5 min; on the evaluation halves the oracle reaches 0.9 in 20 of 20 splits up to L = 14 and in 4 of 20 at L = 16; on the calibration halves it reaches 0.94 in 20 of 20 splits up to L = 10, 12 of 20 at L = 12 and 0 of 20 from L = 14. The frontier study at target 0.94 met the per-history requirement for every rule in 20 of 20 splits at noise 0.005 (B3 belief 19 of 20 at 0.01). The posterior-median rise ratio after the 30-min command is 0.0121, 0.0839 and 0.3264 at 20, 30 and 60 min; its rising branch crosses the measured 0.0409 at 24.46 min (35.5-min shift-equivalent); no posterior sample has a rise ratio below 0.160 at 60 min.
pre_freeze_checks: Before freezing, independent design reviews computed on split r = 0 (noise 0.005; reporter-visible variants also at 0.01): the onset distribution and oracle success by lag; model-calibrated outcomes of the B3-belief, 16-min smoothed, current and fixed rules under hidden lags 0-36 min; threshold-only and threshold-plus-delay recalibration at lags 4-16 min; slack quantiles; slow-subset sizes and outcomes; reporter-visible lag and slowdown variants with effective sample sizes; and they re-ran b3_waiting_frontier for split 0. The lag grids, the feasibility rule, the delay-recalibrated arm, the visible-lag scenario and the onset cuts were set with that knowledge. The split-0 values are not reported as results; the 20-split run below is the only full run.

hidden_lag.lags_min: model-calibrated arm: 0, 2, ..., 40 (scoring only; decisions unchanged); recalibrated arms: 2, 4, ..., 16
hidden_lag.definition: after the 30-min command the plant's outcome at decision time tau is the model's outcome at tau - L (failure for tau < L); reporter observations, the 3-min history and all references are unchanged, so no estimate can reveal the lag

visible_lag.definition: after the 30-min command the plant's noise-free reporter at tau is the model's at tau - L (held at its tau = 0 value for tau < L) and its outcome is the model's at tau - L (failure for tau < L); the split's observation draws are added to the plant reporter; references unchanged, so plant trajectories leave the B3 family; the 3-min history is unchanged

slow_posterior_tail.definition: plants restricted to the posterior samples whose readiness onset after the 30-min command (never ready = +infinity) is >= 90 min (498 of 1000; nominal slowest 50%) or >= 98 min (252 of 1000; nominal slowest 25%); each threshold is the grid value whose realized share is closest to the nominal fraction; the 15 never-ready samples belong to both subsets; the same sample indices in both histories
slow_posterior_tail.meaning: a posterior centred too fast (parameter uncertainty of the population-mean model, not cell heterogeneity); the subset is also slower after the 3-min command; in the model-calibrated arm this is a subgroup analysis of the baseline decisions, with the model correct for every plant

arms.model_calibrated: rule parameters chosen on calibration samples with the model's outcomes (identical to the baseline choices), scored on evaluation plants with the plant's outcomes
arms.outcome_recalibrated: rule parameters re-chosen per history on calibration samples scored with the plant's outcomes (hidden and visible lag: all calibration samples, with the plant reporter in the visible lag; slow tail: calibration samples in the subset); estimators and references unchanged; threshold-only, so limited by the 0.99 grid maximum
arms.outcome_recalibrated_delay: as outcome_recalibrated, but current, smoothed and B3 belief probe at min(first threshold crossing + delta, 120 min) with delta in {0, 2, ..., 40} min chosen jointly with the threshold (and the smoothing scale) per history; if the estimate never reaches the threshold the probe is at 120 min; ties: smaller calibration completion, then smaller delta, then smaller scale, then smaller threshold; fixed waits as in outcome_recalibrated; a different rule family, so its baseline-scenario results are reported as its own reference
arms.oracle: first decision time at which the plant's outcome is a success
arms.idealization: both recalibrated arms use the complete outcome curves of all calibration receivers at every decision time and a common lag; an experiment gives one probe outcome per cell, so they bound what recalibration from measured probes can achieve

feasibility: per split, scenario and lag: a cell is infeasible for the model-calibrated arm if the evaluation oracle misses 0.9 for either history, and infeasible for recalibration at target t if the calibration oracle's success after the 30-min command is below t; rules are compared there on success and completion only and the cell is reported as 'task infeasible', not as a rule failure

outputs.per_split: for every split, noise, scenario, lag or subset, arm and target: per-history and pooled evaluation success and mean failure-penalized completion of fixed, current, smoothed and B3-belief rules and the oracle; whether each rule met 0.9 for both histories; paired differences (B3 belief - fixed, smoothed - fixed, B3 belief - smoothed); gap closure; chosen parameters including delta; feasibility flags
outputs.slack: at baseline, per rule and history on evaluation plants: 5/10/25/50% quantiles of slack = decision time - the plant's model readiness onset (never ready = -infinity) and the share with slack >= L for L = 0, 2, ..., 40 min
outputs.ess: median and quartiles of the effective sample size 1/sum(w^2) of the B3-belief weights at 60 and 90 min after the 30-min command on evaluation plants, per scenario, lag and noise
outputs.summary: over the 20 splits, as in b3_waiting_frontier plus target_reached_on_calibration per rule and history and the number of feasible splits
outputs.descriptive: (a) oracle success within 120 min per history over all samples for hidden lags 0, 2, ..., 40 min, and the model-calibrated success after the 30-min command of every rule over the 20 splits at the same lags; (b) shift-equivalent of the measured mixed probe at the 4% level (descriptive, not an estimate of the readiness delay): median over the 1000 samples of the per-sample ratio rise / naive rise after the 30-min command (readiness tables), crossed on its rising branch by the stored measured median (natural_probe_results.json, probes/fgf_mixed_25ng/pulse_3/rise_over_naive/measured_median); the last decision time before 60 min at which the curve is at or below the measured value, linear interpolation to the crossing, shift = 60 min minus the crossing; the same for the first 3/20 probe after the 3-min command (fgf_3_20_25ng/pulse_2, crossing on the 3-min-history curve, shift = 20 min minus the crossing; negative means B3 recovers too slowly); the minimum and 1% quantile over samples of the 60-min ratio after the 30-min command; (b2) median and interquartile range of the natural-probe rise statistic of the mixed probe under no response: a flat reporter plus white noise of s.d. equal to the stored measured noise floor of fgf_mixed_25ng, on the measured frame times, 100,000 draws, seed 20261010, divided by the stored measured naive median; reading: if the measured median lies inside that range, the shift is reported as 'at least the shift-equivalent; no recovery at 60 min is not excluded'

primary: noise 0.005 and calibration target 0.94; noise 0.01 for the visible-lag comparison of the B3 belief and smoothing; all other cells are secondary, reported in full, and not used in the abstract or the contribution list

statements.M1: hidden lag, model-calibrated arm: tolerated lag per rule = the largest L on the 2-min grid such that the rule meets 0.9 for both histories in >= 16 of 20 splits at every lag <= L; with the median success after the 30-min command per lag; read as differences in slack, next to each rule's baseline completion gain over the fixed waits
statements.M2: visible lag, model-calibrated arm, per lag and noise (0.005 and 0.01): D = [S_B3(lag) - S_B3(baseline)] - [S_smoothed(lag) - S_smoothed(baseline)] per split with S the success after the 30-min command; the B3 belief is the more robust if D > 0 in >= 16 of 20 splits, smoothing if D < 0 in >= 16, otherwise no consistent difference; with the B3 effective sample size and the paired completion difference
statements.M3: hidden and visible lag, outcome-recalibrated arms at feasible cells: splits in which each rule meets 0.9 for both histories; median paired completion difference of the B3 belief and smoothed rules against the recalibrated fixed waits and the number of splits in which each is faster, over splits in which both rules reached the target on calibration for both histories (count reported)
statements.M4: slow posterior tail: per subset, splits meeting 0.9 for both histories per rule in the model-calibrated and outcome-recalibrated arms; per history, the paired per-split difference in subset success (each adaptive rule minus fixed waits) and the number of splits in which it is positive; subset oracle success as ceiling

reporting_templates.T1: Under a recovery lag hidden from the reporter (target 0.94, noise 0.005), fixed waits kept the per-history requirement up to {Lf} min and the current, smoothed and B3-belief rules up to {Lc}, {Ls} and {Lb} min; the measured probe corresponds to a shift of at least {Ld} min, at which the oracle succeeds for {o}% of receivers within 120 min.
reporting_templates.T2: Recalibrated on true outcomes with a delay after the threshold crossing, feedback met the requirement in {n} of 20 splits up to {L} min and stayed {dT} min faster than recalibrated fixed waits.
reporting_templates.T3: When the reporter reveals the lag (B3 effective sample size {ess}), the B3 belief was {more/less/not consistently more} robust than smoothing ({k} of 20 splits) at noise {noise}.
reporting_templates.placement: T1 enters the abstract and Contribution 2; Contribution 3 is restated as conditional on recovery timing being right within the tolerated lag; the onset-split result and descriptive (b) are cross-referenced as the same cells, not independent evidence

checks: baseline: choices identical (JSON equality) and every success, completion, paired difference and gap closure within 1e-12 of waiting_frontier_results.json for all splits, noises and targets; hidden lag and slow tail: estimator probabilities, model-calibrated choices and decision indices identical to the baseline; hidden lag: short-history choices and outcomes identical to the baseline in all arms, model-calibrated success after the 30-min command equal to the share of evaluation plants with baseline slack >= L and non-increasing in L, oracle decision = baseline oracle decision + L if <= 120 min, else failure; slow tail: model-calibrated outcomes equal to the baseline per-plant outcomes restricted to the subset; threshold-only recalibration at lag 0 on the full sample set equal to the baseline; leakage: inverting the outcomes of evaluation plants leaves every recalibrated choice unchanged; one split recomputed from scratch; on any failure no result is interpreted, the failure is recorded, and a corrected version is frozen before the single rerun
reporting: All results reported whatever their direction; simulation of one published model structure with stylized recovery errors, not evidence about measured cells. No rule is described as model-free; the only rule without B3 outputs is the outcome-recalibrated fixed wait. Gap closure, completion differences and 'faster' counts are headline quantities only for rule-split pairs in which both rules meet the per-history requirement; otherwise they are reported and flagged. Near the 120-min horizon completion no longer penalizes failures (D = 120 + W), so for lags of 12 min or more success is the primary outcome. A pure time shift is the most favourable reading of one sub-threshold probe; a slowed recovery rate fitted to the same point would place readiness beyond the 120-min horizon. The 3/20 probe suggests the opposite error after short pulses, which costs time rather than reliability and is not modelled. Reporter-level misspecification under correlated noise is covered by b3_ar1_likelihood; the condition map (feedback delay) is not re-evaluated under mismatch. No bootstrap intervals are computed.
